findings.rule: REVIEW.md Framework rules: 'Flag when the change has made CLAUDE.md outdated' and 'The second occurrence of the same finding across reviews produces a one-line entry in CLAUDE.md ... proposed in the review for the owner'
findings.summary: CLAUDE.md's Layout entries for sample_pkg/calc.py (line 22) and sample_pkg/__init__.py (line 23) still list only add, divide and percent, so the guardrail file is now outdated about the package's public API now that mean ships, and this is at least the second time this exact pattern has been flagged (change 0001 for percent, and already twice within change 0002's own review history per changes/.review-seen.json), which should produce a proposed one-line 'Things Claude gets wrong' entry for the owner.

mean's Collection[float] hint does not stop a str or dict from being passed (both are Collections): a str raises a confusing TypeError from sum() and a dict silently averages only its keys while ignoring values, and neither caveat is mentioned in the docstring, though this is an explicitly decided and already-reviewed contract so the doubt is only about whether it deserves a doc note.
